@graph.headline: Student Travel Safety Tips
@graph.alternativeHeadline: How students studying abroad can travel safely
@graph.description: Safety guidance for students traveling abroad, including pre-departure preparation, health and medical considerations, in-country safety practices, and how travel insurance supports students.

audience.audienceType: College and university students studying abroad, gap year students, exchange program participants, and their parents.

@graph.name: How to Stay Safe While Studying Abroad
@graph.description: A step-by-step preparation guide for students traveling internationally for study abroad programs.

step.name: Register with the State Department's STEP program
step.text: Enroll your trip with the U.S. State Department's Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) so the nearest embassy can contact you in an emergency.

step.name: Get a travel insurance plan with medical coverage
step.text: Purchase a Travel Guard plan that includes emergency medical expense coverage and medical evacuation — most U.S. health insurance plans do not cover you abroad.

step.name: Make copies of your important documents
step.text: Make digital and physical copies of your passport, visa, insurance policy number, and emergency contact information. Store one set separately from the originals.

step.name: Save 24/7 emergency assistance contacts
step.text: Save the Travel Guard 24/7 emergency assistance number (800-826-5248) and the local U.S. embassy contact in your phone before departure.

step.name: Research local safety conditions
step.text: Review the State Department's travel advisories for your destination and your university's program-specific safety guidance before you go.
